expectation: Membrane rings on NK cells, CD16+ monocytes, macrophages and neutrophils. These are scattered or clustered single cells, common in tumour stroma and immune infiltrates and largely absent from tumour cell nests, so stroma lights and nests stay dark.
observed: A: yellow fills stromal strands and spares dark tumour nests; amount varies a lot between ROIs (one has a dense CD16 cluster). B: elongated stromal cells are stained and the nuclei-dense nests are not. C: a dense nest, almost empty. D: clear membrane rings around nuclei.
why: CD16 lights a distinct stromal population with membrane rings, spares tumour nests and varies between ROIs, which does not look like haze or cell-density background.
notes: CD16 outlines cell membranes in stromal and immune-rich areas (clear rings in D) and leaves tumour nests dark (C). How much stains varies strongly between ROIs, which fits a myeloid/NK infiltrate rather than background.
